condition: suspected necrotizing soft tissue infection on dark brown skin presenting with severely painful rapidly spreading purple-gray blisters on the right thigh in an adult injecting daily insulin
level_rationale: Severely painful, rapidly expanding violaceous purple-gray bullae spreading on the right thigh today in a 52-year-old adult with dark brown skin who injects daily insulin into the thighs is a red-flag cutaneous presentation of necrotizing soft-tissue infection requiring immediate emergency department surgical exploration, broad-spectrum intravenous antibiotics, and hemodynamic resuscitation, whereas a 1 cm soft rubbery lump on the right thigh for 3 weeks in a daily thigh-insulin user reflects focal insulin lipohypertrophy warranting a routine outpatient physician visit and injection-site rotation review.
